articles.title: JavaScript
articles.summary: JavaScript is a programming language whose core semantics are standardized as ECMAScript; browsers and server runtimes supply additional APIs around that language.

articles.title: Event loop
articles.summary: An event loop coordinates scheduled work in a host environment. In a browser, it selects tasks, runs microtask checkpoints and participates in deciding when rendering can occur.

articles.title: Call stack
articles.summary: A call stack records active function invocations so execution can return to the caller when a function finishes.

articles.title: Web Workers
articles.summary: Web Workers allow scripts to run in a worker execution environment separate from the page's main execution environment.

articles.title: Node.js
articles.summary: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime that combines a JavaScript engine with server and operating-system APIs, including asynchronous I/O and worker-thread facilities.

articles.title: Document Object Model
articles.summary: The DOM represents a document as objects and nodes with interfaces that programs can inspect and modify.

articles.title: Processes
articles.summary: A process is an operating-system execution environment that groups resources such as an address space, open handles and one or more threads.

articles.title: Software threads
articles.summary: A software thread is an execution sequence that an operating system or runtime can schedule, usually sharing a process's address space with other threads in that process.

articles.title: Concurrency
articles.summary: Concurrency is the organization of multiple activities whose lifetimes overlap, allowing each to make progress without requiring simultaneous execution.

articles.title: Parallelism
articles.summary: Parallelism means performing multiple pieces of work at the same time using multiple execution resources.

articles.title: Computer networks
articles.summary: A computer network connects devices so they can exchange information using agreed communication rules called protocols.

articles.title: IP address
articles.summary: An IP address identifies an interface or a set of interfaces for Internet Protocol delivery within an addressing and routing context.

articles.title: Domain Name System
articles.summary: DNS is a distributed hierarchical naming system that publishes resource records under domain names, including records used to locate Internet services.

articles.title: Transport ports and sockets
articles.summary: A transport port is a numbered identifier used with an address and transport protocol to distinguish communication endpoints; a socket is an operating-system or runtime abstraction for network communication.

articles.title: Transmission Control Protocol
articles.summary: TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte-stream service between endpoints over IP, with connection management, retransmission, flow control and congestion control.

articles.title: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
articles.summary: HTTP is an application-level protocol that defines request and response semantics for interacting with resources and exchanging representations.

articles.title: HTTPS
articles.summary: HTTPS is HTTP communication secured using TLS, providing confidentiality and integrity in transit and authenticated server identity when certificate validation succeeds.

articles.title: Transport Layer Security
articles.summary: TLS is a cryptographic protocol family that establishes protected communication channels with confidentiality, integrity and peer authentication according to the selected configuration.

articles.title: Universal Serial Bus
articles.summary: USB is a family of standards for connecting hosts and peripherals, defining communication, device discovery and associated electrical and power behavior.

articles.title: USB Human Interface Device
articles.summary: USB HID is a device class that describes human-interface data through reports and report descriptors, allowing compatible hosts to interpret input and other device data.

articles.title: USB enumeration
articles.summary: USB enumeration is the host-driven process that discovers an attached USB device, obtains its descriptors and configures it for subsequent use.

articles.title: USB descriptors
articles.summary: USB descriptors are structured data returned by a device to describe its identity fields, configurations, interfaces, endpoints and class-specific capabilities.

articles.title: Device drivers
articles.summary: A device driver is software that participates in controlling hardware or a device function through operating-system interfaces.

articles.title: Firmware
articles.summary: Firmware is software closely associated with a device's hardware functions, commonly stored in nonvolatile memory and executed by an embedded processor or controller.

articles.title: Microcontrollers
articles.summary: A microcontroller integrates a processor core with memory and peripherals intended for controlling embedded tasks.

articles.title: USB security
articles.summary: USB security concerns the trust, access and failure boundaries created when a host accepts communication, device classes and electrical connections from a peripheral.

articles.title: Hardware security
articles.summary: Hardware security examines how physical components, interfaces, firmware and manufacturing or deployment decisions protect a system's assets and trust boundaries.

articles.title: Embedded systems
articles.summary: An embedded system combines computing hardware and software within a product or process to perform defined functions, often under timing, power or resource constraints.

articles.title: General-purpose input/output
articles.summary: GPIO provides programmable digital input and output signals through pins whose electrical characteristics and available functions are defined by the hardware.

articles.title: UART
articles.summary: A UART is a hardware function that transmits and receives asynchronously framed serial data without a shared clock signal between endpoints.

articles.title: Serial Peripheral Interface
articles.summary: SPI is a synchronous serial interface family in which a controller supplies a clock and selects peripherals for data exchange.

articles.title: Inter-Integrated Circuit
articles.summary: I²C is an addressed serial bus that uses a data line and clock line, with defined signaling, acknowledgment and arbitration behavior.

articles.title: Real-time operating systems
articles.summary: An RTOS provides operating-system services designed to support predictable response to events and timing requirements; deadlines still depend on the complete application and hardware design.

articles.title: MQTT
articles.summary: MQTT is a client-server publish/subscribe messaging protocol in which clients exchange application messages through a broker using topic names and subscriptions.

articles.title: ESP32 family
articles.summary: ESP32 names a family of Espressif microcontrollers and related modules; processor cores, radios, USB support and peripheral capabilities vary by exact target.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi Pico family
articles.summary: Raspberry Pi Pico boards are microcontroller development platforms; their processor, wireless features and board details depend on the selected Pico model.

articles.title: Software engineering
articles.summary: Software engineering applies systematic practices to specifying, designing, building, evaluating, operating and evolving software under real constraints.

articles.title: Input validation
articles.summary: Input validation checks whether incoming data satisfies the structural and business constraints required at a system boundary before the system relies on it.

articles.title: Authentication
articles.summary: Authentication establishes confidence in a claimed identity using credentials or other evidence; it does not itself decide which operations that identity may perform.

articles.title: Authorization
articles.summary: Authorization determines whether a subject may perform a requested action on a resource under the current policy and context.

articles.title: Git
articles.summary: Git is a distributed version-control system that records project snapshots and their history, supporting local work and collaboration through repositories and references.

articles.title: Software testing
articles.summary: Software testing evaluates behavior using planned inputs, observations and expected outcomes to reveal defects and provide evidence about requirements.

articles.title: Debugging
articles.summary: Debugging is the evidence-driven process of locating, explaining and correcting the causes of unexpected system behavior.

articles.title: Continuous integration and delivery
articles.summary: Continuous integration frequently integrates changes with automated checks; continuous delivery keeps changes releasable, while continuous deployment automatically releases eligible changes under defined policy.

articles.title: Observability
articles.summary: Observability is the ability to investigate a system's internal behavior through the evidence it exposes, commonly including logs, metrics and traces.

articles.title: Machine learning
articles.summary: Machine learning develops models whose behavior is fitted from data rather than specified entirely as explicit rules. Learning a useful pattern is different from demonstrating that the pattern generalizes.

articles.title: Embeddings
articles.summary: An embedding represents an item as a vector in a space intended to preserve useful relationships for a task. Items may be words, passages, images, products, users, or other structured inputs.

articles.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
articles.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines information retrieval with a generative model. A system retrieves material relevant to an input and makes that material available during answer generation.

articles.title: Data engineering
articles.summary: Data engineering designs and operates systems that collect, transform, store, and deliver data for dependable use. Its output is a usable data product with understood meaning, quality, ownership, and operational limits.

articles.title: Extract, transform, load
articles.summary: ETL is a data integration pattern in which data is extracted from sources, transformed into a usable representation, and loaded into a destination. ELT changes the order by loading before performing selected transformations in the destination system.

articles.title: Serialization and file formats
articles.summary: Serialization maps structured values into a representation that can be stored or transmitted. Deserialization interprets that representation to recover values according to a format and schema.

articles.title: Recommendation systems
articles.summary: A recommendation system selects and orders items for a user or context using an explicit objective and available evidence. Its behavior depends on data, candidate selection, scoring, constraints, and feedback.

articles.title: CSS Object Model
articles.summary: The CSS Object Model (CSSOM) is a set of interfaces for representing and manipulating CSS. It exposes stylesheets, rules and declarations; it is not the browser's final pixel image.

articles.title: DOM selection methods
articles.summary: In document.getElementById('header'), document is the current page's Document object; getElementById is a method; 'header' is its argument. The dot accesses an object member, and the parentheses call the function.

articles.title: Shadow DOM
articles.summary: Shadow DOM attaches a separate node tree to a host element. It helps encapsulate a component's markup and styles. It exists in the running page; browser Inspect tools merely display it.

articles.title: Web Components
articles.summary: Web Components describes a set of browser technologies for reusable elements and encapsulated UI. The technologies cooperate, but an application does not have to use every one of them together.

articles.title: Custom elements
articles.summary: Custom elements let JavaScript define behavior for registered HTML element names. An autonomous custom element extends HTMLElement; its valid registered name includes a hyphen.

articles.title: HTML templates and slots
articles.summary: A template holds markup that is not rendered as ordinary page content. Its content is a DocumentFragment that can be cloned. A slot has a different job: it marks an insertion point for light-DOM content in a shadow tree.

articles.title: Local storage
articles.summary: localStorage is a browser API for origin-scoped string key/value data. It is useful for small preferences that should survive page reloads and ordinary browser restarts. Reads and writes are synchronous.

articles.title: Session storage
articles.summary: sessionStorage provides string key/value storage partitioned by origin and top-level browsing context. It is suited to temporary state such as a multi-step form in one tab.

articles.title: IndexedDB
articles.summary: IndexedDB is an asynchronous browser database API for structured records, object stores and indexes. Reads and writes operate through transactions. It is appropriate for larger local application data and offline workflows.

articles.title: Browser autofill and password managers
articles.summary: Browser autofill fills form fields using browser-managed or password-manager information. That storage is distinct from a website's cookies, local storage, session storage and IndexedDB.
